summary: Kickoff between Redwood AE/SE and Helion (Procurement, Legal, CTO, Finance, Security) to align contract, pricing, and technical gates for a pilot within Helion's ML incubator. Main topics: DPA redlines, egress/ residency constraints, SLA needs for hosted vs dedicated inference, pricing thresholds, and next steps to run a short benchmark. General tone cooperative but cautious — Helion has strict residency requirements for patient-derived data and a finance review window in two weeks.
topics: Onboarding path for ML incubator (tech ridealong and benchmark)
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-10-28 16:00 PDT
Duration: 49 minutes
Attendees: Alex Martinez (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Helion Procurement), Maya Patel (Helion Legal), Samir Gupta (Helion CTO), Elena Ruiz (Finance), Tom Chen (Security)
Recording: https://app.redwood.example/meetings/ff-20251028-helion-mlinc-001 (note: placeholder)

Summary (auto): Align on DPA redlines, pricing, and pilot acceptance criteria.

[00:00] Alex Martinez: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate you making time. quick intros?
[00:10] Jordan Lee: Jordan here, procurement; we run vendor intake for Helion's incubator, i'm the procurement owner on quick timeline.
[00:16] Maya Patel: Maya, legal, i'll own reviews for DPA / MSA redlines.
[00:22] Samir Gupta: Samir, CTO for the incubator, i'll be hands on for the pilot, want to validate latency and cost numbers.
[00:29] Elena Ruiz: Elena, finance, we'll sign off on pricing if the numbers fit our pilot budget.
[00:34] Tom Chen: Tom, security, quick lens on residency and keys.
[00:38] Alex Martinez: Great, alex with Redwood, and priya from our infra team is with me; goal is to understand constraints and agree next steps for onboarding.

[02:05] Priya Shah: Quick technical context. Redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC options; we usually recommend hosted for speed to value, dedicated for consistent p99, private when you need customer-managed networking.
[02:39] Samir Gupta: For us, a lot depends on data residency. we'll be testing with patient-derived imaging text metadata in the incubator; can you support EU-only or US-only residency? also curious about using our KMS.
[03:02] Priya Shah: Yes, we provide region pinning and KMS integrations for dedicated/private offerings. for hosted, we can pin region and we do support customer-managed keys via our KMS integration on Private. small caveat: hosted with BYOK is in preview for some regions, but Private and Dedicated fully supported.

[04:25] Maya Patel: On the DPA, there are three clauses we need clarity on: data retention windows, subprocessors list and notification timing, and an egress charge cap. also will need audit log access for a 12 month window.
[04:48] Alex Martinez: understood. we can share our standard DPA and mark the subprocessors list; we typically provide 30 day notice for subprocessor changes and can negotiate audit retention. egress — we'll flag pricing tiers and any caps.

[06:10] Jordan Lee: timeline question — procurement needs a decision for pilot funding in two weeks. is that realistic to get contract terms and a pricing number?
[06:21] Alex Martinez: yes, provided legal redlines are minor. we'll send a pricing spreadsheet after this call and propose a pilot SOW.

[07:40] Elena Ruiz: how do we think about cost projection? Samir's team will run 100k tokens/day for a 4 week pilot likely. rough number?
[08:00] Priya Shah: rough: hosted with batching could be lower cost but p99 varies; dedicated gives predictable throughput. i'll run an estimate after Samir shares exact qps and prompt lengths.
[08:21] Samir Gupta: typical prompt length ~350 tokens, responses averaging 150 tokens, peak concurrency ~20 reqs/sec.

[09:12] Tom Chen: security wise we need SOC2 status and a list of encryption at rest/in transit options, plus whether Redwood has HSM/KMS integrations for customer keys.
[09:29] Alex Martinez: we have SOC2 Type II and provide KMS integrations; Private supports HSM via partner KMS. i'll attach our security pack.

[11:03] Maya Patel: a specific redline: we need to cap egress fees for regulatory data; Helion can't accept open-ended egress. any flexibility?
[11:18] Alex Martinez: we can cap egress in the SOW for the pilot and propose a tiered egress allowance. for long-term contracts we typically define egress tiers or a negotiated cap.

[13:40] Jordan Lee: procurement also wants to know rollback and SLA credits — example if p99 latency spikes during a clinical demo.
[13:55] Priya Shah: we have SLA templates for latency and availability; for mission-critical demos the recommendation is dedicated with canary rollouts and automatic fallback to a smaller model variant. credits are in the MSA.

[15:30] Samir Gupta: curious about caching — can Redwood preserve KV cache across sessions to reduce cold start for few-shot prompts?
[15:45] Priya Shah: yes, we do KV/prefix caching and it can be configured per route; that reduces token costs and latency for repeated prompt patterns.

[18:00] Elena Ruiz: finance question on billing granularity — do you bill per token, per request, or hybrid for dedicated?
[18:12] Alex Martinez: hosted is per-token plus optional request units; dedicated is reserved capacity (monthly commit) plus overage per token. we will provide a modeled cost sheet for the pilot.

[20:20] Maya Patel: legal also needs indemnity and data processing addendum alignments for EU data if we cross borders; we're leaning towards dedicated in-region if numbers work.
[20:38] Alex Martinez: makes sense — for EU-resident data we recommend dedicated or private pinned to EMEA region.

[22:10] Jordan Lee: do you support SSO and SAML for onboarding user access?
[22:19] Alex Martinez: yes SAML SSO supported, RBAC for teams, and token-level auditing in the console.

[24:01] Tom Chen: can we do a short security questionnaire? we have a 30-question vendor security assessment; prefer to fill an RFP doc.
[24:12] Alex Martinez: absolutely, we'll assign our security reps and fill out. i'll put that as an action item.

[26:40] Priya Shah: technical next step: we propose a 1hr ridealong to run a sample workload against hosted and dedicated variants so we can produce latency and cost deltas.
[27:02] Samir Gupta: yes please, schedule that. we'd like to see p50/p95/p99 and token cost per 1k in both setups.

[29:15] Elena Ruiz: procurement — what's typical lead time for dedicated pool provisioning?
[29:24] Priya Shah: typically 2-4 weeks depending on region and capacity, pilot dedicated can be expedited in some regions.

[31:00] Maya Patel: legal note — we'll request a 30 day notice for subprocessor changes and prefer 12 month audit log retention. also need clarity on data deletion mechanics post-pilot.
[31:16] Alex Martinez: data deletion flow is documented; we'll include deletion certificates for pilot data if needed.

[33:42] Jordan Lee: procurement timeline reminder — we need signed pilot SOW and pricing approved within two weeks (approx Nov 11) for internal funding windows.
[33:55] Alex Martinez: understood; we'll prioritize the redlined DPA and a pilot pricing sheet this week.

[35:20] Priya Shah: practical step — Samir, please share a sample payload and rough QPS distribution. i'll prepare a benchmarking plan.
[35:32] Samir Gupta: will do, i'll try to get a sample by end of week.

[37:10] Alex Martinez: quick Q&A — Maya, any no-go clauses we should know now?
[37:20] Maya Patel: nothing absolute yet, but egress caps, KMS integration for keys, and audit logs are high priority.

[39:00] Elena Ruiz: finance asks whether there's a pilot discount or credit for initial month?
[39:12] Alex Martinez: yes, we can offer pilot credits and a discounted pilot rate — details on the pricing sheet.

[41:25] Tom Chen: security follow-up — will you provide an SOC2 report and vulnerability disclosure policy?
[41:33] Alex Martinez: yes, attaching SOC2 Type II and vulnerability disclosure.

[43:50] Priya Shah: ok next steps recap — we'll send DPA, pricing, security pack; schedule ridealong; Helion provides sample workload and timeline.
[44:05] Jordan Lee: noted. procurement will circulate internal forms.
[44:12] Maya Patel: legal will do initial redlines and push back on egress text if needed.
[44:20] Samir Gupta: i'll get the qps and payload by Monday.

[45:30] Alex Martinez: thanks everyone; i'll follow up with the items and attach the docs. if no objections we'll target pilot kickoff week of 11/10 pending redlines.
[45:50] Jordan Lee: good thanks.
[46:00] Meeting ended.
